agent.problem: Too many choices are discoveries or coin flips for informed guesses to be the majority. Stop 1 card 5 asks about redemption in Babylon right after only the destination was established; stop 1 card 11 gives no basis for deciding who gets the wealth; stop 1 card 13 introduces the struck judge only in the question; and stop 2 card 3 introduces the ruler's eternal origins only in the question. Added to the picture, destination and town discovery questions, a baker using only the earlier cards must guess on about half of the choices.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Two important positive facts are never actually taught. Stop 1 card 11 only lets the baker reject keeping the wealth; no card says Zion devotes the gain to the LORD and the wealth to the Lord of all the earth (Micah 4:13). Stop 2 card 7 only rejects shepherding in His own strength; no card says He shepherds in the strength of the LORD and in the majestic name of the LORD His God (Micah 5:4).

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: "Those peoples" has no antecedent within the question and points back to story card 10, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify them as the peoples Zion breaks to pieces or the nations gathered against her.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
